hints: Compare switch S open with no current to switch S closed with current through resistor R.
Recall that e.m.f. $E$ is work per unit charge done by the battery, while terminal p.d. $V$ is what remains for the external circuit.
Think where $V = E - Ir$ loses energy when current $I$ flows through the internal resistance.
walkthrough: With S open there is no current, so there is no potential drop inside the battery and the potential difference across its terminals equals its e.m.f.
When S is closed, a current $I$ flows around the loop through R and also through the internal resistance $r$ of the battery.
The e.m.f. $E$ is fixed by the chemistry of the battery and does not change when current flows.
Part of $E$ is now used to do work against the internal resistance, giving lost volts $Ir$, so terminal p.d. is $V = E - Ir$.
Therefore $V$ across the battery is smaller when S is closed because of work done against internal resistance. This is option C.

options.A: The e.m.f. does not fall when S is closed. It is a fixed property of the battery.
options.B: The e.m.f. stays constant and work done in R produces the terminal potential difference, not a fall in e.m.f.
options.C: Closing S gives current $I$, so $Ir$ is lost inside the battery and terminal p.d. $V = E - Ir$ falls.
options.D: Work done in R accounts for the energy delivered to the external circuit, not the lost volts inside the battery.
